name: Quake3e
description: Native PS5 port of Quake3e, the improved Quake III Arena engine, drawing with Vulkan at up to 4K with DualSense or USB mouse and keyboard input. Needs your own Quake III Arena game data.
author: Gary Riches
release_notes:
Mouse and keyboard support: plug a USB mouse and keyboard into the console and play as on a desktop, beside the DualSense.

Added
- A USB mouse: look, the menu pointer, MOUSE1 to MOUSE5 and the wheel, bound as the game binds them by default (fire on the left button, zoom on the middle, the weapons on the wheel).
- A USB keyboard: Quake's own keys (W, A, S and D, the number keys and the rest of the default binds), typing into the console, a chat line and the menus' text fields, with key repeat. The key left of 1 opens the console.
- A mouse speed slider in Setup, Controls. It changes the mouse alone; the horizontal and vertical sensitivities, invert look and smooth look are the stick's and the mouse's alike.
- The cvars in_ps5Mouse, in_ps5MouseSpeed and in_ps5Keyboard.

Changed
- Setup, Controls shows a pad button and a mouse or keyboard key side by side for an action, and takes a mouse button, the wheel or a key as a bind. A new bind takes the place of one of its own kind, so the pad's stays.
- With a keyboard plugged in, only the pad (CROSS or TRIANGLE) opens the on-screen keyboard.

Tested, and not
Seen on one console on 2026-10-11: a USB mouse's movement, three buttons and wheel, and a USB keyboard connecting with its keys read.

Not yet verified: the mouse speed slider, a mouse's side buttons, and a Bluetooth mouse or keyboard. The status table is kept current.

Known limits
- The keyboard types the US layout's characters, whatever the keyboard's own.
- The mouse and keyboard are read while a controller is connected.
- The controls menu shows two binds for an action; others stay bound and are not shown.
- The game modules run in the bytecode interpreter; there is no JIT yet.
- No fast (HTTP) downloads: servers that need extra pak files are slow to join.
- No Ogg Vorbis music.

Install
You need a PS5 that already runs homebrew (an enabler such as etaHEN, ShadowMountPlus, and an FTP server) and your own Quake III Arena data.
- Download Quake3-PS5-v1.1.0.zip below and unzip it: it holds one folder, PPSA99303.
- Put pak0.pk3 (from a copy of the game you own) and pak1.pk3 to pak8.pk3 (the 1.32 point release, from https://ioquake3.org/extras/patch-data/) in PPSA99303/baseq3/.
- Copy the folder to the console over FTP as /data/homebrew/PPSA99303/.
- Launch "Quake III Arena" from the home screen.

Updating from 1.0.0: copy the new folder over the old one; your game data and settings stay.

The README has the details. No game data is included.
